parent_self.text: When my child talks, I stop what I'm doing and listen.
I tell my child "I love you" or "I'm proud of you."
I notice when my child is upset and check in.
I'm curious about my child's interests and friends.
When my child does well, I praise something specific.
We have relaxed time to chat together every week.
After a mistake, I comfort my child before we discuss it.
My child can safely tell me about their worries.
I often look at my phone while my child is talking.
When my child cries or gets angry, I say they're overreacting.
I rarely know what's been bothering my child lately.
When I'm angry, I say hurtful things to my child.
I set clear family rules together with my child.
When I set a rule, I explain why.
I have clear, reasonable expectations about my child's schoolwork.
I follow up on whether my child does what they agreed to.
I know where my child is after school and who they're with.
I expect my child to help with chores.
We have a screen-time agreement and we stick to it.
When a rule is broken, I respond the way we agreed beforehand.
If my child pushes hard enough, I usually give in.
Our rules change depending on my mood that day.
I don't usually ask whether my child's homework is done.
If my child stays up very late, I usually let it go.
